thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-api-us-west p95/p99 latency spike detected. queue_length=642, gpu_pool_util=99%, autoscaler=ERROR (provisioner quota denied). page: oncall-sre :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: ack — seeing the alert. joining now. what's the initial impact?
runtime-engr: hitting `ProvisionerRateLimit: quota_exceeded` when creating GPU instances. stack snippet from provisioner: ```
Error: ResourceQuotaExceeded
at Provisioner.createInstances (/srv/provisioner/main.go:482)
message: "quota exceeded for region us-west-2: g4dn-family"
```
prod-support: customer-ops reports 504s for a handful of tenancies, some retries. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 3.6s, p99 -> 18s. customers: a few high-traffic SaaS partners.
oncall-sre: confirmed 504 spike and backend timeouts. Hosted queue is growing, retention bucket filling. any evictions or OOMs?
infra-oncall: no OOMs in hosts, just can't provision new pods. cloud account is returning 429/quota errors. looks like quota enforce kicked in at ~5987654305.
ops-lead: tagging this P1. impact: degraded for ~12% of requests to hosted API in us-west. routing to eu still healthy.
runtime-engr: autoscaler attempted 8 scale-ups in last 7m, all failed. current pools: 0 spare GPUs. fallback policy should route to smaller model or CPU fallback; enabling now for low-priority traffic.
prod-support: can we throttle non-PLG traffic? or reduce batch sizes? customers on Dedicated unaffected.
oncall-sre: action plan: 1) enable fallback routing to cpu/lightweight models for non-critical routes, 2) reduce batch target to lower token concurrency, 3) open quota request and if not immediate, manually spin smaller-GPU SKUs. who's owning quota request?
ops-lead: I'll open cloud support & entitlement case. copying billing for quota uplift. link: https://cloud.console/quotas/request-case/ABCDE
runtime-engr: applying fallback now. command:
```
./infractl set-routing --region us-west --policy fallback-to-cpu --scope low-priority
```
runtime-engr: applied, starting to see queue drain from low-priority tenants. queue now 412. p95 dropped to 1.2s.
customer-ops: posting update to affected customers: "We're routing lower-priority requests to a CPU fallback to keep service available. You may see increased latency for non-critical workloads."
prod-support: prod dashboard: error_rates: 504s reduced by 40% after fallback, but some high-cost model requests still queued.
infra-oncall: cloud support replied: quota increase estimated >24h. no expedited.
oncall-sre: we need temporary capacity. options: a) scale up smaller-GPU SKUs (g5a) that are under a different quota, b) burst in another region and route traffic, c) continue fallback. pros/cons?
ops-lead: (a) quickest is to provision g5a in us-west if available. requesting permission to override instance SKU policy.
prod-support: note: some customers pin models requiring specific GPU family; fallback won't help them. we should identify pinned customers and surface CS playbook.
runtime-engr: manual reprovision attempt to g5a hitting different quota too but lower usage. I'll try `infractl provision --sku g5a.xlarge --count 6` now.
runtime-engr: provision accepted for 6 g5a.xlarge. instances booting. queue drops to 210. p95 ~420ms.
oncall-sre: nice. keep monitoring for regressions. watch for thermal throttling on new hosts.
customer-ops: updated customers in channel: "We've provisioned temporary alternative capacity and enabled fallback for lower-priority traffic. Full quota request is in with cloud — ETA 24h+. We'll follow up." :white_check_mark:
ops-lead: assign runbook follow-ups: - postmortem owner? - inventory pinned customers - add warning in dashboard when autoscaler fails due to quota
nightshift-sre: I'll take on postmortem authoring and the pinned customer list. handing off to night shift at 00:30 UTC.
oncall-sre: handing off. key things for night shift: keep fallback enabled, monitor queue <300, watch p99 < 2s, escalate to infra-oncall if queue >500 or new provision failures.
infra-oncall: adding monitoring alert: `autoscaler.provision_errors` -> pager if >5 in 10m (currently 12).
prod-support: log note for customers: paste incident stub into STATUS page.
oncall-sre: timeline notes to add: detection 5987654289, autoscaler first error 5987654295, quota enforce 5987654305, fallback enabled 5987654328, manual g5a provision success 5987654360.
runtime-engr: logs saved to s3://redwood-incident-logs/5987654321/ for postmortem. include `provisioner` traces.
ops-lead: close loop: we still want automated SKU diversification in autoscaler to prefer SKUs with headroom. adding ticket.
customer-ops: customer impatience is cooling — monitoring support tickets.
nightshift-sre: taking over monitoring now. ping me in this thread for urgent updates.
oncall-sre: leaving channel, thanks all. :pray:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity -> P1 -> mitigated (partial). notes: queue reduced, manual capacity added, quota request pending.
post-incident action items (inline): - owner: nightshift-sre -> postmortem due in 72h - owner: runtime-engr -> autoscaler SKU diversification RFC - owner: infra-oncall -> escalate quota process with cloud account manager - owner: prod-support -> customer comms follow-up and credits if needed
